en.title: Relative clauses
en.summary: A relative clause adds information about a noun.

paragraphs: A relative clause adds information about a noun. It begins with who, which, that, whose, where or when.

items: The man **who lives next door** is a doctor.
The book **that I read** was long.
This is the town **where I was born**.

paragraphs: A defining clause says which one and has no commas. A non-defining clause adds extra information and is set off by commas: My brother, who lives in Leeds, is a nurse.
